title: Exporting the animatic and swapping in final renders
content:
The last step for the animatic is to export it as a video you can watch, share and get feedback on. Then, because you named and organized everything carefully, the same After Effects edit can become your final animation: render final frames from Blender and swap them in for the animatic's, and your cuts, sound and titles stay as they are. You'll need the edit from the last part.

Export the animatic

  1. Send it to Adobe Media Encoder. 0:02 To make a video for Vimeo or YouTube, or for someone to review, add the composition to Adobe Media Encoder's queue (File → Export → Add to Adobe Media Encoder Queue). Media Encoder opens, and the composition shows up in its queue after a moment 0:08.

  2. Choose a preset and where to save it. 0:27 The video uses the Vimeo 1080p Full HD preset (H.264); you can choose another. Click the output file to choose where it goes: the project's videos folder keeps everything straight 0:39. Name it (here, animatic-2) and click Save 0:51.

  3. Start the queue. 0:56 Click the green start button to render a video file you can stream.

  4. Watch it. 1:30 Open the new file, for example in QuickTime, and play it through.

  5. Use it to make decisions. 1:59 The point isn't that you've made the world's best animation, but that you've blocked it out so you can decide things. How fast should the character come out? Is the sound working? What else needs animating to make it come alive? You'll spot other problems too, like a loop that doesn't loop as well as you hoped 2:24.

Render the final frames

  1. Plan to reuse the edit. 2:41 With this much work in the animatic, the final edit is nearly done: you can replace the animatic's renders with final renders, as long as the frame ranges and timing don't change 2:52.

  2. Point the scene at a new folder. 3:45 In Blender, set up the scene for its final render quality (here, EEVEE with lighting and materials), then change its output folder so you don't overwrite the animatic renders 3:55. Make a new folder, either a final-renders folder or one named for the scene with something like FINALRENDER added 4:08. It's the same scene, with its animation finished and final render settings 4:25.

  3. Render the animation. 4:46 This time, instead of a viewport render, choose Render → Render Animation. It uses the scene's full render settings and writes the image sequence into the new folder 4:55. Here the animation isn't finished, so the result is somewhere between an animatic and a final render 5:09.

Swap the footage in After Effects

  1. Open the After Effects project. 5:31 The video switches to the project the Part 1 animatic was made from, so its edit is different from the last part's 8:59.

  2. Reconnect missing footage. 6:20 If files have moved, footage shows as missing (color bars). Right-click it in the Project panel and choose Replace Footage → File 6:33. Go to the right folder, select the first image, check PNG Sequence is ticked and click Open 6:48. Reload Footage may find it on its own; here it didn't.

  3. Replace each sequence with its final render. 7:21 If you can point missing footage at a folder, you can point any footage at a different one. Replace each animatic sequence with the same shot from your final renders, selecting the first image as before 7:35. All your edits stay as they were, now with the final frames 7:42. Go down the list and replace them all 7:51.

  4. Reconnect the audio and preview. 8:59 Missing audio is reconnected the same way; once one is found, After Effects may find the others in the same folder 9:07. Then preview it 9:40.

  5. Export it the same way. 10:46 Choose File → Export → Add to Adobe Media Encoder Queue, pick the folder and start the queue, and you have your final animation file.

10:25 As long as you don't change too much, swapping in final frames saves a lot of time. That's the whole process 11:03: blocking the animation, setting up cameras and scenes, slowing shots down with time remapping to give yourself choices in the edit, and editing in After Effects with opacity and sound levels, titles and credits.
